memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'These are the LORD's appointed festivals, which you are to proclaim
as sacred assemblies for bringing food offerings to the LORD - the
burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings
required for each day. These offerings are in addition to those for
the LORD's Sabbaths and in addition to your gifts and whatever you have
vowed and all the freewill offerings you give to the LORD'"
- Lev 23:37-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here God summarises the whole calendar. And notice the last line:
these festival offerings were in addition to the weekly Sabbaths, the
personal gifts, the vows and the freewill offerings.

In other words, the festivals were the framework, not the whole of
worship. There was still room for spontaneous, personal, voluntary
giving to God whenever the heart moved.

Dear friend, that balance is worth learning. Some believers live
entirely by structure - Sunday service, daily reading plan, set prayer
times - but rarely turn to God spontaneously. Others live entirely by
impulse, praying only when they feel like it, and their spiritual life
rises and falls with their mood.

God gave Israel both. Fixed appointments that did not depend on
feelings, and freewill offerings that flowed from a moved heart.

The early church shows the same pattern. They devoted themselves to the
apostles' teaching, to fellowship, to breaking bread and to prayer
(Acts 2:42) - and they also praised God spontaneously and shared as
anyone had need.

Build the structure. Then leave room for the Spirit to move you beyond
it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I more structured or more spontaneous in my walk with God - and
   what is missing?
2. What fixed rhythm would strengthen my faith right now?
3. When did I last worship God simply because my heart moved me to?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, give me faithful rhythms that hold me steady and a heart that
still runs to You freely. Let both be worship that pleases You. Amen.
